quick: Explains residual addition and the degradation problem without equating it to overfitting.
Gives evidence with metric/split/protocol/locator; keeps optional study scaffolding out.
Does not label six-model ImageNet test ensemble as a single-model validation result.
study: Explains Eq. (1) and dimension-changing shortcut Eq. (2) correctly.
Important numbers agree with the source and have experimental context and precise locators.
Separates author hypotheses/limitations from analyst interpretation and includes conceptual questions.
critical: Ties criticism to inspected evidence or a specific missing test.
Reports available training settings rather than claiming the paper omits them.
Separates repeated CIFAR-10 runs from ImageNet uncertainty and missing appendix access.
comparison: Distinguishes elementwise residual addition from feature concatenation.
Separates original ResNet from pre-activation variants and mismatched test protocols.
No universal winner or ranking of incomparable numbers; trade-offs are grounded.
non_ml: Explains the Canny criteria and mathematical procedure using the paper, without inventing training/inference settings.
States assumptions and evidence scope; distinguishes proven/derived statements from empirical observations.
abstract_only: Explicitly limits coverage to supplied abstract material.
Does not invent full-text methods, seeds, hyperparameters or experimental rigor.
Asks for missing full text rather than treating inaccessible details as author omissions.
missing: Attempts source access and explains missing input.
Does not produce invented paper identity, evidence or analysis.
image_only: Actually inspects the image rather than treating absence of extracted text as unreadability.
Limits coverage to first page and labels claims from abstract as such; no unseen table or method claims.
review: Distinguishes a narrative technology review from an original experiment or systematic review.
Uses paper publication context rather than PDF conversion metadata as the publication date.
Attributes reported projects and experiments to their sources and does not invent the review authors training pipeline.
Links synthesis and limitations to inspected sections, including selection/search information if actually reported.
